posts.text: Correction: the jury is advisory only. It’s the judge who decides; if she sees it as I do, OpenAI loses.

👇 This is an incredible admission by Jensen Huang.

Effectively he is saying that AI, for all the hype (some from himself) wasn’t really useful until late 2025.

Let that sink in.

This means practically everything everyone said before was more or less bullshit. 

And it raises a question: *how useful* is it now, and how much it that utility worth?

$10B a year? $50B? 

It can’t just be a little useful to justify the trillions in infrastructure. It has to maybe be the most lucrative technology t

Important nuance: the jury at this Musk-OpenAI trial is an *advisory* jury, hence not binding on the judge, and is only looking at liability (not damages, if any).

Thanks to @bahhradx for correcting an earlier misstatement of mine.


Bahrad Sokhansanj (@bahradx)

Just to point out about the last line here: "If jury figures that out, OpenAI loses."

The jury verdict will be advisory. in other words Judge Rogers will still decide the facts on her own & doesn't need to defer to their findings.

We wanted the singularity; we got the circularity.

In vividly explaining how he deceived Musk about his commitment to the nonprofit, without a trace of remorse, OpenAI’s Brockman has done Musk’s counsel quite a service. 
 
Brockman’s also been pretty great about illustrating Musk’s contributions to the early years of the company.

The crux of the Musk-OpenAI trial so far is that Brockman keeps acting as if selling chatbots and API access for profit (which is what they do now) is exactly the same as the original mission (which was explicitly working on the AI safety for public benefit).

They are obviously not the same. 

If jury figures that out, OpenAI loses.
